233446934_5d0fb07e.text: A large hypothalamic structure, the MPOA sends projections to multiple downstream brain regions and is both larger and contains more neurons in males than in females [35]. Notably, the MPOA is home to various heterogeneous, molecularly defined, neuronal clusters, including many sexually dimorphic populations, such as androgen receptor (AR)-expressing population and estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1)expressing population [80]
233446934_5d0fb07e.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

233446934_8cb6b0bc.text: Another molecularly defined sexually dimorphic VMHvl subpopulation that controls sex-typical behaviors in both sexes is the progesterone receptor (PR)-expressing neurons. This subpopulation is required for the normal display of mating in both sexes and for fighting in males [76].
233446934_8cb6b0bc.section: Sexually Dimorphic Brain Regions and Structures

233446934_9f0f55ea.text: At least two different subpopulations within the MPOA were shown to be required for the regulation of pupdirected behavior. The first is the ESR1 þ population, which is highly sexually dimorphic in its distribution and projection patterns [85]
